cards.explanation: The answer is pride. Isaiah says they speak "With pride and arrogance of heart…" (Isa 9:9). Their city has taken a hit, and they answer with a building upgrade. Friends, I once told a cookie that it was my best work while it sat there burnt on one side, so I know that kind of talk. Isaiah just names it plainly.

The answer is Philistia. Isaiah says, "Aram from the east and Philistia from the west have devoured Israel with open mouths." That's one nation on each side, and Philistia is the one on the west. I think this is a heavy picture, and Isaiah gives it to us plainly.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, "Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised." (Isa 9:12). Aram and Philistia have already come with open mouths, and the anger hasn't turned away. "Despite all this…" is Isaiah's way of saying there's more still to come in this passage.

The answer is True. Isaiah says, "…the people did not return to Him who struck them; they did not seek the LORD of Hosts." They got struck, and they still didn't turn back or go looking for Him. Two lines, friends, and both say they didn't.

The answer is the prophet who teaches lies. Isaiah says the head is the elder and honorable man, and "…the tail is the prophet who teaches lies." I think a prophet who teaches lies is a hard thing to read about. The verse names both parts of the picture, so nobody has to guess.

The answer is mislead. Isaiah says, "For those who guide this people mislead them…" Then he adds that "…those they mislead are swallowed up." That's a guide leading people the wrong way. It's like following a map to the bakery and ending up at a parking lot, friends, except this one is far more serious.

The answer is that every one of them is godless and wicked. Isaiah says, "For every one of them is godless and wicked, and every mouth speaks folly." That's the reason the verse gives, and it covers the young men, the fatherless and the widows. I won't add any reasons of my own to it.

The answer is wrath. Isaiah says, "By the wrath of the LORD of Hosts the land is scorched, and the people are fuel for the fire." It's a heavy verse and I won't joke over it. Wrath is the word the text uses, friends, and I'll leave it at that.

The answer is hungry. Isaiah says, "They carve out what is on the right, but they are still hungry; they eat what is on the left, but they are still not satisfied." They keep eating and they are still hungry. I think that's a heavy line, so I'll let it stand.

The answer is Judah. Isaiah says, "Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they turn against Judah." Judah is the one they turn against together. It's a rough picture, friends, and Isaiah doesn't soften it.

The answer is the poor. Isaiah says those laws are made "…to deprive the poor of fair treatment and withhold justice from the oppressed of My people…" These are the unjust statutes and oppressive decrees he just named (Isa 10:1), and the poor and the oppressed are who they're aimed at. It's a serious thing, so I'll just say it plainly.

The answer is True. Isaiah says they do it "…to make widows their prey and orphans their plunder." I think this one hurts. The text names widows and orphans, friends, and I'll stay quiet and let the words stand.

The answer is that no one can rescue them. Isaiah asks, "To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?" and he leaves no answer in the verse. I think that empty space is the point. A question with no helper in it is a heavy thing to hear.

The answer is captivity or death. Isaiah says, "Nothing will remain but to crouch among the captives or fall among the slain." Those are the only two things he lists. It's the hardest line in this stretch, friends, so I'll say it plainly and leave it there.
